turns.user: I need published mortars with drying shrinkage no more than 600 microstrain at 28 days and compressive strength of at least 50 MPa.
turns.text:
I’ll search for published mortars with both properties reported at 28 days and check the matching mixes.

The database contains matching measurements. One paper uses negative strain for contraction, so I’m checking shrinkage magnitudes and excluding net expansion from the shortlist.

Yes. These published mortars meet both limits in the literature database, with **both measurements recorded at 28 days**.

| Mix | Composition summary | Drying shrinkage magnitude (microstrain) | Compressive strength (MPa) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| OPC-6 | OPC with siliceous river sand | 565 | 61 |
| EX-6 | 85% OPC + 15% CSA-based expansive additive | 150 | 65 |
| EX-L-6 | Same binder; 20% of sand replaced by expanded-clay lightweight sand | 125 | 69 |
| EX-L-0 | Same composition as EX-L-6; different curing | 222 | 59 |

All have **w/b = 0.40** and **sand/binder = 2.60**. Source: [published study, Table 4](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2017.12.001).

The “-6” mixes received **6 days of moist curing**, followed by drying at **23 ± 1 °C and 50 ± 3% RH**; EX-L-0 received no initial moist-curing period. Strength used **50 mm cubes, ASTM C109**; shrinkage followed **ASTM C157**. The paper records contraction as negative strain; the table shows its magnitude.

Additional UHPC mixes classified as mortars in the database also qualify:

| Mix | Drying shrinkage (microstrain) | Compressive strength (MPa) | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| GOS50 | 574 | 120.03 | [Waste glass/oyster-shell powder study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jobe.2024.109833) |
| J3 | 411 | 109.4 | [Shrinkage-reducing and expansive admixture study](https://doi.org/10.1155/2017/6384859) |

**EX-6 and EX-L-6 are useful starting candidates.** These are extracted published measurements; confirm whether “28 days” means specimen age or drying duration before adopting a mix, and verify experimentally under your curing conditions.

input.sql: SELECT p.paper_uid AS doi, p.title, p.year, m.mix_uid, m.name_in_paper AS mix, m.w_b_reported, m.sand_binder_ratio, s.value_canonical AS shrinkage_microstrain, c.value_canonical AS strength_MPa, s.source_locator AS shrinkage_source, c.source_locator AS strength_source, s.fig_only AS shrinkage_fig_only, c.fig_only AS strength_fig_only, s.condition_note AS shrinkage_condition, s.notes AS shrinkage_notes, ts.standard AS shrinkage_standard, ts.notes AS shrinkage_test_notes, tc.comparability_group AS strength_specimen, m.curing_regime FROM mixes m JOIN papers p ON p.paper_uid=m.paper_uid JOIN measurements s ON s.mix_uid=m.mix_uid JOIN measurements c ON c.mix_uid=m.mix_uid LEFT JOIN tests ts ON ts.test_uid=s.test_uid LEFT JOIN tests tc ON tc.test_uid=c.test_uid WHERE m.system_type='mortar' AND s.quantity='drying_shrinkage' AND CAST(NULLIF(s.age_norm_d,'') AS REAL)=28 AND s.unit_canonical='microstrain' AND CAST(NULLIF(s.value_canonical,'') AS REAL) BETWEEN 0 AND 600 AND c.quantity='compressive_strength' AND CAST(NULLIF(c.age_norm_d,'') AS REAL)=28 AND c.unit_canonical='MPa' AND CAST(NULLIF(c.value_canonical,'') AS REAL)>=50 ORDER BY p.paper_uid, m.mix_uid
